title: Build an IB Business Management Study Group That…
summary: Build an effective IB Business Management study group for September-November with focused roles, weekly agendas, case practice, and accountability.
body_markdown:
An effective **IB Business Management study group** is small, structured, and centred on visible evidence of learning. From September to November, aim for **3-5 reliable members** , meet weekly for 60-75 minutes, and finish each session with completed questions, corrected calculations, an essay plan, or an updated error log.


Business Management is not mainly a note-sharing subject. Students must recall knowledge, apply it to unfamiliar cases, analyse consequences, evaluate trade-offs, and communicate justified conclusions. Group meetings should therefore move quickly from brief review to independent practice and correction.


### Choose reliable members and clear rules


Invite students who attend consistently, prepare beforehand, accept correction, and attempt questions independently. Members do not all need to be achieving a 7. A mixed-ability group can work well when everyone explains their reasoning and contributes evidence.


Keep the group to **3-5 students** . This is practical advice, not an IB requirement. At the first meeting, agree that:


- Meetings start and finish at fixed times.
- Everyone completes the assigned preparation.
- Phones remain away during focus blocks.
- Every session produces a measurable output.


Use one communication channel for agendas, resources, attendance, and necessary questions. Avoid allowing it to become an unfocused social chat.


### Match practice to IB assessment


The course covers five units: introduction to business management, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing, and operations management. It also integrates the concepts of **change, creativity, ethics, and sustainability** with business tools and theories.


The official[SL subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/business-management-sl-subject-brief-en.pdf) explains that Paper 1 uses a pre-released statement and unseen case study, while Paper 2 has a quantitative focus. The[HL subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/business-management-hl-subject-brief-en.pdf) adds Paper 3, based on unseen stimulus about a social enterprise.


Your group should practise four abilities:


- **Recall:** definitions, formulas, theories, and toolkit components
- **Application:** linking knowledge to precise case evidence
- **Analysis:** explaining consequences for objectives and stakeholders
- **Evaluation:** weighing trade-offs and reaching a justified judgment


Reading notes together may improve familiarity, but it does not show that members can perform these tasks independently.


### Follow a September-November plan


Adapt the topics to your school's teaching order, while preserving the progression from diagnosis to timed performance.


Period Main purpose Group output


September, weeks 1-2 Diagnose weaknesses Baseline quiz and priority lists


September, weeks 3-4 Secure terminology and theories Retrieval quiz and short responses


October, weeks 1-2 Improve application and analysis Marked case-based paragraphs


October, weeks 3-4 Strengthen quantitative work Corrected problem set


November, weeks 1-2 Develop evaluation Timed extended response


November, weeks 3-4 Consolidate learning Mixed test and error-log retest


Select narrow targets such as motivation theories, break-even analysis, market research, or production methods. The[RevisionDojo Business Management hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management) can provide a shared syllabus-aligned structure.


### Use a repeatable meeting agenda


A consistent agenda prevents meetings from becoming casual conversations.


Time Activity Required output


0-5 minutes Set the objective One topic, skill, and output


5-15 minutes Closed-book retrieval Individual answers


15-25 minutes Teach-back Brief explanation with an example


25-45 minutes Exam-style practice Independent writing or calculation


45-60 minutes Compare and correct Identified marks and omissions


60-70 minutes Record and assign Updated error log and preparation


Rotate the roles of **facilitator** , **timekeeper** , **skeptic** , and **scribe** . The skeptic asks which case evidence supports a claim or which limitation affects the judgment. The scribe records recurring misconceptions rather than complete answers for others to copy.


Independent attempts are essential. If one confident student explains every answer, other members may feel they understand without learning to produce responses themselves.


### Practise subject-specific skills


Use the[Business Management Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management/questionbank) to choose a common topic, but require everyone to answer before discussion. For qualitative questions, identify the command term, select a relevant theory or tool, apply precise case evidence, explain consequences, consider limitations, and reach a conditional judgment when evaluation is required.


For quantitative questions, write the formula, substitute values, show working, include units, and interpret the result in context. A correct calculation without business interpretation is incomplete preparation.


Use[Business Management Flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management/flashcards) between meetings for definitions and formulas. Reserve meeting time for application, calculation, argument, and correction, where peer discussion adds more value.


### Build accountability


Before each meeting, assign a small task such as five flashcards, one attempted question, and one point of confusion. Track preparation, attendance, attempts, and corrections without publicly ranking members.


If someone misses preparation twice, discuss it privately. If the pattern continues, reduce the group size. Consistent participation matters more than having many members.


### Protect academic integrity


The Business Research Project is an **individual assessment** at both SL and HL. Members may discuss concepts, research methods, source reliability, and assessment expectations, but they should not exchange finished paragraphs or create shared analysis for submission.


The IB[academic integrity policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/shared-resources/pdfs/academic-integrity-policy-en.pdf) requires authentic work and prohibits undue assistance. Discuss approaches together, then research and write independently. Follow your teacher's instructions whenever the boundary is unclear.


Jojo AI may explain a theory, create a practice scenario, or comment on an independently written practice response. It should not replace student authorship. RevisionDojo's guide to[integrity in IB Business Management](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/integrity-in-ib-business-management-ethical-strategy-and-authentic-analysis) offers further guidance.


### Avoid common study-group mistakes


Replace vague goals such as “revise marketing” with measurable tasks. Keep peer explanations brief, then require retrieval or application. Always correct completed questions and rewrite weak sections.


Use diagnostic results to schedule avoided skills, especially calculations. Treat predicted papers as timed practice, not forecasts of exact examination content. The guide to[earning a 7 in Business Management](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-ib-business-management) explains how to combine content repair, application, quantitative work, and timed responses.


### Conclusion


A productive fall study group needs reliable members, a fixed weekly agenda, rotating roles, and tasks aligned with IB assessment. Progress from diagnosis and terminology to case application, quantitative interpretation, evaluation, and timed practice.


RevisionDojo can support this structure without replacing individual responsibility. Use Study Notes and Flashcards before meetings, the Questionbank for shared practice, and Jojo AI after an independent attempt for targeted feedback.
